 Live .  4,298 viewing 4298 viewing Championship: Birmingham go top, West Ham lose at Blackburn, Cardiff beat Burnley 5-4 from 4-1 down
 Live Reporting (active) 
 Scores 
 Tables 
 Summary
 West Ham lose 2-1 at Blackburn, bottom side Preston beat Southampton
 Cardiff come from 4-1 down to beat Burnley 5-4 in stunning fightback
 Birmingham hit late goal to beat Swansea and go top, WBA brush aside Millwall
 Also wins for Charlton and QPR, Boro held at Watford
 Earlier, Wrexham 1-1 Wolves, Norwich win 5-0 at Bristol City, Stoke come from behind to beat Portsmouth
 Get Involved: Use yellow button
 Close form Send us your views
 Get involved Live Reporting
 Kate Holloway, Alex Hoad, Ben Kosky and Deepak Mahay
 Most recent Most popular Merry-go-round at the top published at 17:21 GMT 17:21 GMT 
 Championship 
 Image source, Opta/Shutterstock What a day. Told you it would be special.
 Four teams sat top of the Championship at various points today, but it's Birmingham who go into the international break on top.
 Wolves were top for just two minutes at lunchtime before being pegged back in a draw at Wrexham.
 Stoke took over for an hour or so after coming from behind to win at Portsmouth but Middlesbrough's game against Watford took Boro back to first, where they stayed until Birmingham went ahead against Swansea, and then returned there for 22 minutes when the Swans equaliser.
 However Jay Stansfield's winner three minutes from time has Birmingham top of the pile, but with fifth-placed West Brom only a point behind after their 3-0 win over Millwall.
 Southampton and West Ham suffered painful defeats in Lancashire to fall off the pace while at the other end Charlton picked up a vital win to move seven points clear of the drop-zone and rock-bottom Preston closed the gap with their second win, but Burnley remain five points adrift after their stunning 5-4 defeat at Cardiff, having been 4-1 up.

 Full-time headlines published at 17:19 GMT 17:19 GMT 
 Championship 
 Birmingham go top on goal difference after Jay Stansfield's double earns them a 2-1 win over 10-man Swansea
 Middlesbrough are held 0-0 at Watford while Stoke climb to third after a 2-1 lunchtime victory at Portsmouth
 Wolves miss their chance to hit the summit after being held to a 1-1 draw at Wrexham
 Cardiff come from 4-1 down to edge a nine-goal thriller at home to Burnley, with Alex Robertson scoring an injury-time winner
 Jordan Thompson's strike secures a surprise win for bottom side Preston against in-form Southampton - their first under Graham Alexander
 Blackburn hold on to beat West Ham 2-1 at Ewood Park, the visitors' fourth game without a win

 Limbs at the Cardiff City Stadium published at 17:15 GMT 17:15 GMT 
 FT Cardiff 5-4 Burnley 
 Mark Poyser 
BBC Radio Wales commentator at Cardiff City Stadium 
 Even the people in the directors box to my left lost control of their bodies during the culmination of one of the most remarkable afternoons I've ever witnessed.
 Cardiff were 4-1 down just past the hour mark after Alex Robertson put past his own goalkeeper.
 The Australian would go from zero to hero by curling home an exceptional winner from distance in stoppage time.
 There was pandemonium in the Canton Stand as the Bluebirds maintained their unbeaten home record.
 This is why we love the game of football.

 It wasn't a poor performance, it was good performance.
 The frustration is that Middlesbrough just couldn't put the ball into the back of the net.

 FT: Birmingham 2-1 Swansea 
 Colin Tattum 
Former Birmingham City media officer on BBC Radio WM 
 Blues are looking like the real deal. I know it's a long way to go but this group of players seem to find a way to win.
 There is something about this Blues team under Chris Davies.

 FULL-TIME published at 17:04 GMT 17:04 GMT 
 Cardiff 5-4 Burnley 
 Image source, Shutterstock Madness.
 It seemed like it was over for Cardiff when Burnley went 4-1 up but having conceded a point from a three goal comeback from West Ham earlier in the week, they knew it wasn't over.
 Yousef Salech proved a great substitution after scoring a double, one in his first minute on the pitch, as well as earning a penalty for Jack Moylan to tuck away.
 It was Alex Robertson, who had earlier scored an own goal by diverting in a cross, that won it for them with an absolutely stellar strike.
 That's a first loss for Burnley boss Fabio Celestini. Much to unpack for him - and Bluebirds boss Brian Barry-Murphy, in fairness.

 FULL-TIME published at 17:04 GMT 17:04 GMT 
 Birmingham 2-1 Swansea 
 Image source, Getty Images Birmingham just take victory against 10 man Swansea to go top of the Championship table.
 They extend their undefeated run at home to 11 games after Jay Stansfield sealed his double with an 87th minute set-piece goal.
 Swansea made them work for it though after a corner turned of Christoph Klarer's thigh to ruin the three-game run of clean sheets at St Andrew's.

 Birmingham 2-1 Swansea 
 Birmingham boss Chris Davies has a very attacking team on the pitch now in a bid to take this win but Swansea will want to take advantage of that.
 They are pushing for a late equaliser as Jenson Seelt's header is blocked.
 Nervous home supporters around the ground right about now.

 FULL-TIME published at 17:00 GMT 17:00 GMT 
 Preston 1-0 Southampton 
 A first clean sheet since February for Preston.
 Just a second blank in 35 games for Saints.
 The Championship strikes again.
 Jordan Thompson's first-half rocket ensures just a second win of the season for rock-bottom Preston who rode their luck and defended valiantly in the second half to hold on.
 The Saints miss the chance to get right among it at the top of the table.

 'Watford deserve point' published at 16:59 GMT 16:59 GMT 
 FT: Watford 0-0 Middlesbrough 
 Derek Payne 
Former Watford midfielder on BBC Three Counties Radio 
 The fans understand that they've come up against a very good team in Middlesbrough and they'll have to defend.
 I'm not going to paper over the cracks but the fans will appreciate the hard work and effort. They deserve a point.
 I'm very pleased for Alessio Dionisi and the players have shown that they are playing for him today.

 Birmingham 2-1 Swansea 
 There is eight minutes added.
 Birmingham are heading to the top of the table as it stands and with just 10 men, you fancy their chances of staying there.

 FULL-TIME published at 16:57 GMT 16:57 GMT 
 Charlton 2-1 Sheff Utd 
 Image source, Shutterstock Nathan Jones and Charlton breathe a sigh of relief as Will Mannion makes a last-gasp save to deny Sydie Peck the equaliser.
 The 11-match winless streak is over.
 Millenic Alli is the hero, scoring the first goal before the break, and after Jordan Ayew had nodded the leveller after a flap from Will Mannion, Alli produced a wonderful assist for fit-again Matty Godden to hook home the winner 11 minutes from time.
 Blades lose ground on the play-off places while the Addicks move away from the basement.

 QPR 2-1 Lincoln 
 Glen Kamara's late winner makes the difference and stretches QPR's undefeated home record to five games.
 Richard Kone headed Rangers into an early lead before Dom Jefferies levelled for the Imps, who have now lost their last three games.

 GOAL: Cardiff 5-4 Burnley published at 16:56 GMT 16:56 GMT 
 Alex Robertson (90 + 4 mins) 
 Alex Robertson has made up for that own goal now.
 Having accidentally found the net up the other end, he thunders home up the other end to give Cardiff a potential winner.
 Superb strike. Worthy of winning but in this game, who knows?!

 FULL-TIME published at 16:54 GMT 16:54 GMT 
 Watford 0-0 Middlesbrough 
 For all their possession and chances... no goals for Middlesbrough.
 As it stands, they won't be going back to the top of the Championship this evening.
 Watford will be pleased with a point, you'd imagine.
